i.norm: Verifies that when InterpolatorStringLookup is used as a Function via compose(), and the pre-composed function returns null, the overall composed function also returns null. compose(f) builds: input -> interpolator.apply(f.apply(input)) Since f always returns null, interpolator.apply(null) is called, which returns null.
Arrange: create an interpolator backed by the XmlDecoder lookup as its default
Arrange: a mock pre-function that returns null for any input
Act: compose the interpolator with the null-returning function, then apply to a key compose(f) means: composedResult = interpolator.apply(nullReturningFunction.apply(input))
Assert: because nullReturningFunction returns null, interpolator.lookup(null) returns null
